subject: general-mathematics
title: Laws of indices
summary: Multiply, divide and raise powers, and work with zero, negative and fractional indices.

lesson.text: In a^n, a is the base and n is the index (or power). a^n means a multiplied by itself n times: 2^3 = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

items: Multiplying, same base: add the indices. a^m × a^n = a^(m+n)
Dividing, same base: subtract the indices. a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n)
Power of a power: multiply the indices. (a^m)^n = a^(mn)
Zero index: a^0 = 1 (for any a that is not 0)
Fractional index: a^(1/n) is the nth root of a, and a^(m/n) = (nth root of a)^m

lesson.title: Simplify 2^3 × 2^4
steps: Same base, multiplying: add the indices.

lesson.title: Evaluate 8^(2/3)
steps: The bottom of the fraction is the root: the cube root of 8 is 2.

lesson.title: Solve 2^x = 32
steps: Same base on both sides, so the indices are equal: x = 5.

lesson.text: These laws only work when the bases are the same. 2^3 × 3^2 cannot be combined into one power: work it out instead (8 × 9 = 72).

questions.explanation: Same base, multiplying: add the indices. x^(5+3) = x^8.
A power of 1/2 is the square root. The square root of 16 is 4.
Any number (except 0) to the power 0 is 1.
A negative index means one over: 2^(−3) = 1/2^3 = 1/8. It is not negative.
Cube root of 8 is 2, then square it: 2^2 = 4.
